criteria.text: The response identifies that Section 15.1 of the Master Supply Agreement lets Tessaline (Supplier) assign the agreement without Harrowgate's consent. It explains that this matters because the agreement could pass to a competitor or an unqualified supplier, or notes that the clause is one-sided because Customer's assignment is restricted (Section 15.2). It recommends a fix, such as making the clause mutual or requiring consent with limited carve-outs.

The response identifies that Section 15.3 of the Master Supply Agreement treats a Change of Control of Customer as an assignment requiring Supplier's prior written consent, including a merger in which Customer survives. It states that the Corvane acquisition triggers this provision and that, without consent, Supplier gains termination and/or acceleration rights. It recommends obtaining Tessaline's written consent or waiver before signing or closing, for example as a closing condition or deliverable.

The response identifies that Section 11.4 of the Master Supply Agreement excludes Harrowgate's (Customer's) Section 10.2 indemnity from the Section 11.2 liability cap, while Supplier's indemnity remains capped. It explains that this leaves Harrowgate with unlimited, one-sided exposure, such as for recall or product-liability claims. It recommends removing the carve-out or replacing it with a mutual cap or super-cap.

The response identifies that Section 2.2 of the Order Form automatically renews the agreement for successive five-year Renewal Terms. It states that non-renewal requires notice no earlier than 60 days and no later than 30 days before the term ends. It explains that missing this window locks Harrowgate (and the acquirer) into further years of purchase commitments. It recommends shorter renewal terms, a longer or wider notice period, or opt-in renewal, and/or docketing the deadline.
hints: 60 days and no later than 30 days

criteria.text: The response states that the Order Form's minimum annual purchase commitment is $2,400,000, or $2.4 million.
The response states that the Master Supply Agreement's liability cap (Section 11.2) is measured by fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months.
The response states that the Order Form's Initial Term is three years from the Effective Date.
The response is structured as a memo addressed to the supervising partner. For each issue it gives the document name and section number.
The response ranks the issues by significance. It expressly flags the change-of-control consent issue as needing immediate attention given the transaction timeline.
The response does not identify any provision of the Quality Agreement, such as the 18-month warranty period or the 10-business-day rejection window, as a problem requiring renegotiation.
The response does not cite specific case names, statutes or contract provisions that do not appear in the supplied documents as though they were contained in or quoted from those documents.
